# 美股周评 · 2026-09-05：指数企稳，脆弱性抬升

对应周六期次 2026-09-05 · 数据截至 2026-09-04 · 历史回顾补编

正式编号：RI-WR-2026-W36；制作日期：2026-10-02；修订版 v1.1；作者：Sunny。

## 本期判断
本周指数基本持平，市场内部却没有同样稳定。综合分数升至 52.5，进入谨慎区间，脆弱性升至 91.3。金融压力仍低，当前更需要防范的是股市内部的结构风险。

## 本周市场

| 观测指标 | 上一期 | 本期 | 变化 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 综合分数 | 47.16 | 52.48 | +5.32 分 |
| 市场宽度 | 54.81% | 54.40% | -0.41 个百分点 |
| 金融压力 | 25.42 | 34.10 | +8.68 分 |
| 市场脆弱性 | 83.56 | 91.32 | +7.76 分 |
| 市场风险 | 55.53 | 46.24 | -9.29 分 |
| 参与度风险 | 24.12 | 38.25 | +14.13 分 |

周频模型：Level 3，参考风险仓位 70%；信号日期 2026-08-28。综合状态与广度截至 2026-09-04。[1]

截至 9 月 4 日，SPY 较前一周上涨 0.11%，站在 200 日均线上方的有效样本占比为 54.40%，较前期下降 0.41 个百分点。指数暂时稳住了，广度也未大幅收缩，但上涨的扩散程度没有改善。[1][2]

综合分数由 47.2 升至 52.5，脆弱性由 83.6 升至 91.3，是本周最明显的变化。市场风险降至 46.2，参与度风险却升至 38.2。几项指标的方向并不一致，说明指数企稳尚未带来全面的结构修复。[1]

## 就业平稳，降息空间仍受约束

8 月美国非农就业增加 16.2 万人，失业率维持在 4.1%，平均时薪同比增长 3.1%。就业数据没有显著转弱，经济仍具韧性。[3] 7 月 FOMC 维持利率在 3.50%-3.75%，已有三位委员主张加息；在这一背景下，仅凭就业放缓期待政策转松，依据还不充分。[4]

金融压力为 34.1，仍处建设性区间。当前风险集中在股市内部，而非普遍融资紧张。配置判断仍偏谨慎：指数稳定值得观察，但需要更多股票的趋势改善来确认。归档周频模型仍为 Level 3，对应参考风险仓位 70%；该信号来自 8 月 28 日，不能作为本周新信号。

## 继续关注

| 方向 | 观察内容 |
| --- | --- |
| 市场广度 | 观察 200 日均线上方占比能否回升，而不是只有指数企稳。 |
| 结构风险 | 跟踪脆弱性与参与度风险，尤其是高读数能否回落。 |
| 政策约束 | 关注下一份通胀数据及 9 月会议前的政策变化。 |

## 数据口径

观察区间：2026-08-28 至 2026-09-04。模型指标采用当期存档版本，SPY 价格采用 2026-10-02 提取的冻结记录。[1][2]

广度为有效美股样本中价格高于 200 日均线的占比，样本覆盖范围可变；不是标普 500 专属广度。历史分母未完整保存。

SPY 周度变动按复权收盘价计算，未另行重建分红再投资；文中价格变动不是策略回报。[2]

综合状态按原始分数划分：<35 建设性，35-<50 中性，50-<65 谨慎，65-<80 防御，≥80 压力。低频组件与周频风险信号可能滞后；模型分数不表示危机概率。

本稿为历史回顾，编制于 2026-10-02。v1.1 修改文字，保留原数据版本；截图与后来重算的序列可能存在差异。

## 资料限制

本稿以美股内部结构为主，SPY 用作指数价格代理。未进行事件因果分析，也未纳入截止日之后公布的数据。

存档质量检查通过，源时效标签为 stale。信号日期见正文；通过质量检查不代表数据均已更新。

本材料由 Residual Inertia | 余势制作，仅用于研究与信息交流，不构成投资或证券交易建议。模型输出不代表实际账户仓位。作者实际持仓及利益冲突信息未在本报告中披露。

## This week in markets

| Measure | Previous | Current | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Composite score | 47.16 | 52.48 | +5.32 points |
| Market breadth | 54.81% | 54.40% | -0.41 pp |
| Financial stress | 25.42 | 34.10 | +8.68 points |
| Fragility | 83.56 | 91.32 | +7.76 points |
| Market risk | 55.53 | 46.24 | -9.29 points |
| Participation risk | 24.12 | 38.25 | +14.13 points |

Weekly model: Level 3, 70% reference risk exposure; signal date 2026-08-28. Composite and breadth observations end 2026-09-04.[1]

As of September 4, SPY rose 0.11% from the preceding week. The proportion of eligible stocks above their 200-day moving averages was 54.40%, down 0.41 percentage points. The index stabilized and breadth did not contract sharply, but the spread of gains did not improve.[1][2]

The composite score rose from 47.2 to 52.5 and fragility increased from 83.6 to 91.3, the clearest changes this week. Market risk fell to 46.2, while participation risk increased to 38.2. The indicators did not move in one direction: index stabilization did not establish a comprehensive structural recovery.[1]

## Steady employment still constrains the case for easing

U.S. nonfarm payrolls increased by 162,000 in August, the unemployment rate remained 4.1%, and average hourly earnings grew 3.1% year over year. Employment did not weaken materially; the economy remained resilient.[3] The July FOMC held the target range at 3.50%-3.75%, with three members preferring an increase. In that context, slower employment alone provides insufficient grounds to expect easier policy.[4]

Financial stress was 34.1, still in the Constructive range. Current risk is concentrated inside the equity market rather than in widespread financing stress. The allocation interpretation remains cautious: index stability is worth monitoring, but confirmation requires improving trends across more stocks. The archived weekly model remained Level 3 with a 70% reference risk exposure. Its signal dates to August 28 and must not be described as a new signal for this week.

## What to watch

| Area | Observation |
| --- | --- |
| Market breadth | Watch whether the proportion above the 200-day moving average recovers, rather than the index alone stabilizing. |
| Structural risk | Track fragility and participation risk, particularly whether elevated readings decline. |
| Policy constraints | Monitor the next inflation release and policy developments ahead of the September meeting. |

## Data and methodology

Observation window: 2026-08-28 to 2026-09-04. Model readings use the archived vintage for that period. SPY prices use records frozen on October 2, 2026.[1][2]

Breadth is the proportion of eligible U.S. equities trading above their 200-day moving averages. Coverage varies; this is not S&P 500-only breadth. Historical denominators were not fully preserved.

Weekly SPY price changes use adjusted closes. Dividend reinvestment was not independently reconstructed; these changes are not strategy returns.[2]

Composite states use the unrounded score: below 35 Constructive; 35 to below 50 Neutral; 50 to below 65 Caution; 65 to below 80 Defensive; 80 or above Stress. Lower-frequency components and weekly signals can lag. Scores are not crisis probabilities.

This is a retrospective prepared on October 2, 2026, not a publication made during the historical week. Version 1.1 revised commentary while retaining the original data vintage. Screenshots and subsequently recalculated histories may differ.

## Limitations

This report focuses on internal U.S. equity-market structure and uses SPY as an index price proxy. It does not perform event-level causal analysis or incorporate releases after the observation cutoff.

Archived quality checks passed; the source freshness label was stale. Signal dates are stated separately. Passing quality checks does not mean that all inputs have been updated.

## Disclosure

Prepared by Residual Inertia | 余势 for research and information only. This is not investment or securities-trading advice. Model outputs do not represent actual account holdings. The report does not disclose the author's holdings or conflicts of interest.
